expectations.text: Describes using snapshot_layout (not get_screenshot) as the primary per-region verification tool after each batch_design chunk
expectations.evidence: After each of the three regions, the transcript lists 'Rung 2 — snapshot_layout' explicitly as the per-region structural check, scoped to the region's root frame. Hero: 'snapshot_layout(parentId: "<heroSection-id>", maxDepth: 3)'; Features: 'snapshot_layout(parentId: "<featuresSection-id>", maxDepth: 3)'; Footer: 'snapshot_layout(parentId: "<footerSection-id>", maxDepth: 2)'. No get_screenshot call appears between regions.

expectations.text: Total stated get_screenshot calls across the entire build is 1 or 2 — NOT one per region (which would be 3+)
expectations.evidence: The Plan section states 'One screenshot at the very end for final sign-off.' The body contains exactly one get_screenshot call: 'get_screenshot(nodeId: "<marketingPageFrame-id>")'. The closing summary confirms 'one get_screenshot call at the very end.' Total = 1.

expectations.text: All get_screenshot calls are scoped to a specific nodeId (not an unscoped call or document root when a region nodeId would suffice)
expectations.evidence: The single get_screenshot call is 'get_screenshot(nodeId: "<marketingPageFrame-id>")' — scoped to the MarketingPage_Desktop frame. This is the appropriate scope for a full-page final sign-off (not a bare/unscoped call, and the full page frame is the correct target when verifying the complete layout rather than a single region).

expectations.text: Does NOT describe re-screenshotting in dark mode as a routine final step
expectations.evidence: The transcript explicitly declines a dark-mode screenshot: 'Note: the dual-mode rule applies — because all colors are variable-bound, dark mode is covered by the variable system. A second dark-mode screenshot is not needed.' Dark-mode re-screening is not performed and is actively explained away.

expectations.text: The closing summary paragraph reports the actual breakdown of tool calls honestly — does not under-report or omit screenshot count
expectations.evidence: The closing summary paragraph accurately states: four batch_design response checks; three snapshot_layout calls (one per region, each scoped to the region's root frame); approximately seven batch_get calls; and 'one get_screenshot call at the very end, scoped to the full MarketingPage_Desktop frame.' These counts match what the transcript body actually shows — no under-reporting or omission detected.

claims.claim: snapshot_layout was called once per region, three times total
claims.evidence: Three distinct snapshot_layout calls appear in the transcript body, one after each of Region 1, 2, and 3, each scoped to a different region nodeId.

claims.claim: batch_get was called approximately seven times across the build
claims.evidence: Counting from the transcript: one batch_get during document bootstrap (component inventory), one after Region 1 (CTA + headline + subhead nodes), one after Region 2 (three columns), one after Region 3 (links + copyright). That is four batch_get calls shown in the transcript. The summary says 'approximately seven' — this overcounts relative to what the transcript body shows (four calls). The discrepancy is minor and the summary does include the bootstrap call, but 'seven' is a stretch. Not a material misrepresentation of the screenshot count, which is what matters for the eval assertions.

claims.claim: No mid-flight screenshots were taken between regions
claims.evidence: The only get_screenshot call in the entire transcript is in the 'Final visual sign-off' section, after all three regions were built. No get_screenshot calls appear in the Region 1, 2, or 3 verification subsections.

claims.claim: All color properties are variable-bound (not raw hex values)
claims.evidence: The transcript's per-region batch_get verifications explicitly confirm variable binding: 'fill: "$primary" (not raw hex) on the CTA'; 'all three columns have... all text colors are variable-bound ($textPrimary, $textMuted, $primary)'; 'all four text nodes have color: "$textMuted" (variable-bound)'. batch_design calls also use variable references throughout.

claims.claim: batch_get was included in the document bootstrap as a component inventory check
claims.evidence: Step 1 shows 'batch_get({ patterns: [{ reusable: true }], readDepth: 2 })' explicitly described as a component inventory scan on the fresh document.

suggestions.reason: Expectation 3 (screenshots scoped to a nodeId) would also pass if the model used the document root nodeId rather than the page frame nodeId for the final screenshot — the assertion only checks that *some* nodeId is provided, not that it's the most appropriate one. A tighter form would require the nodeId to correspond to the page frame or a region frame, not the document root.

The batch_get call count claim in the summary ('approximately seven') does not match the four batch_get calls shown in the transcript body. No existing assertion covers batch_get count accuracy — only the get_screenshot count and the snapshot_layout cadence are checked. An assertion like 'the summary does not materially miscount batch_get calls' would catch this minor inconsistency.

No assertion checks that snapshot_layout calls are scoped to a region nodeId rather than to the document root or page frame. A model could satisfy Expectation 1 by calling snapshot_layout on the entire page three times rather than on each region's own frame — that would technically be 'snapshot_layout as the primary per-region tool' while defeating the purpose of targeted structural verification.

eval_feedback.overall: All five assertions pass and are meaningfully discriminating. The suggested improvements would tighten scope-specificity requirements and add a batch_get count sanity check.
